summary: Chess is a pure two-player abstract battle of maneuver and calculation with no luck and no hidden information, where every piece's fixed movement pattern creates a vast space of tactical and positional possibilities. Games range from quick tactical skirmishes to long, tense strategic maneuvering, and outcomes are determined entirely by the players' skill and preparation.
praised: Infinite strategic depth from simple rules
Pure skill expression with zero luck
Enormous body of theory, literature, and community support
Endlessly replayable with no two games alike
Widely accessible and playable at any level from casual to professional
criticised: Steep skill ceiling means mismatched players have little fun
Can be slow and mentally exhausting at longer time controls
Opening theory memorization can feel like a barrier to entry
No hidden information or variance can make it feel dry to some casual players

scoring.why: The game is decided by checkmate, resignation, or draw, not by any point accumulation.
